title: When is the lien released after an Auto Loans payoff?
content:
# When is the lien released after an Auto Loans payoff?

This part of the Auto Loans payoff policy at PCB governs the release of the lien on a paid-off vehicle: the deadline and the way the release is sent.

## Clauses

1. **Deadline.** The lien release must be sent within the product's lien-release period, in business days, after the loan was paid off.
2. **Business days.** Business days are Monday through Friday, excluding Federal Reserve holidays.
3. **Counting.** Count business days with the first business day after the loan's closing (paid-off) date as day 1; the release is due by the business day that ends the count, that day included.
4. **Method.** The release is sent electronically to the state motor vehicle agency where the title is electronic; otherwise the signed title is mailed to the address on file.

After payoff the lien shows as release pending; once the release is sent it shows as released, with the date the release was sent.

## Counting illustration (illustrative period of 3 business days, not a product value)

Paid off on Wednesday 2026-10-21, assuming no Federal Reserve holiday falls in the period.

| Business day | Date |
|---|---|
| day 1 | Thursday 2026-10-22 |
| day 2 | Friday 2026-10-23 |
| day 3 | Monday 2026-10-26 |

| Release sent | On time? |
|---|---|
| Monday 2026-10-26 | yes: on the last day of the count |
| Tuesday 2026-10-27 | no: after the count ends |

**Wrong reading:** "the weekend counts toward the period." **Correct basis:** only Monday to Friday business days count, and Federal Reserve holidays are skipped.

**Which way is the release sent?** An electronic title means an electronic release to the state motor vehicle agency; a paper title means the signed title is mailed to the address on file.
